question.trigger_rationale: Repository ValueSnapshot concatenates deltas, but equality only compares latest_value. Existing sync_test deliberately disconnects and rejoins a lagging node. Use the same public recovery path with full-content equality and FIFO per-link delivery; this distinguishes expanded-base missing-interval loss from correct delta reconstruction. Other frontiers need transport/configuration authority investigation; this one has an immediate public-API content discriminator.

obligation.description: When successful Delta synchronization represents a decided prefix as a snapshot, the snapshot must preserve the complete content of that decided prefix under the application Snapshot semantics, including entries already decided locally before recovery.

scope.description: Successful snapshot-enabled SequencePaxos recovery in a single configuration using correctly implemented create/merge and Storage operations.
assumptions: Snapshot::create represents its supplied ordered entries and merge incorporates subsequent delta entries.
Connected transport preserves per-link FIFO; a disconnected link may lose messages and reconnection is reported.

grounding.derivation: Decided entries must not revert (M-log-contract). Snapshot represents compacted decided entries, and merge combines a local snapshot with subsequent changes (M-storage-contract, M-snapshot-contract). M-value-snapshot demonstrates concatenating delta contents as an in-repository supported implementation. Therefore successful recovery that compacts a prefix must retain its complete decided content, not just its last value.
grounding.applicability: Snapshot-enabled correct create/merge implementation; successful memory storage; one configuration; authentic target-generated messages and FIFO connected links; finite disconnection followed by reconnected notification. No progress deadline or persistent crash claim.
alternatives: A Complete snapshot avoids the Delta merge path. An idempotent last-value oracle can conceal lost earlier content.
